runs.text: Novelis Inc. has become more leveraged because it is funding a USD 5.0 billion plant and recovering from two fires at the same time. Company-defined net leverage was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026, against a management goal of about 3.5x during the investment cycle, which management says tariffs and the fire impacts have pushed above target [financial base; Q2R p65]. Total debt rose by USD 1,819 million in six months to USD 9,797 million, and Adjusted Net Debt rose by USD 1,796 million, almost the same as the USD 1,804 million Adjusted Free Cash Flow outflow, so the extra debt is the cash burn of capital spending and working capital rather than shareholder returns [financial base; RQ2 p9, p10].

Liquidity has narrowed and rests on one facility. The company had USD 2,038 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, down from USD 2,756 million at March 31, 2026, and the revolver availability of USD 606 million is the main committed backstop [financial base; Q2R p19, p61]. The reported figures reconcile to a revolver drawn about USD 2,266 million with USD 128 million of letters of credit against a USD 3,000 million commitment (calculated, see Calculations), which suggests the commitment rather than the borrowing base is the binding limit; that is an inference and the borrowing base is not printed. Short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million are classified as due within one year, although the revolver itself matures on June 16, 2031 [Q2R p17, p18].

Bond maturities are not the near-term pressure. Only USD 13 million of 3.25% notes falls due in November 2026, and the next large maturities are USD 568 million of notes in April 2029, USD 2,350 million across two series in January 2030 and USD 750 million in August 2031 [financial base; Q2R p17]. The term loans mature in March 2032 and a USD 500 million term loan in July 2028. The risk is therefore the cost and availability of bank liquidity through the build, and then the size of the 2029 and 2030 refinancing if leverage has not come down.

Earnings are improving on a reported basis but are definition sensitive. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 1,831 million against USD 1,645 million for fiscal 2026, and the quarter included USD 39 million of business interruption recoveries and favorable scrap effects that management cites [financial base; RQ2 p2]. The measure excludes USD 69 million of trailing start-up costs and USD 1,140 million of trailing fire losses net of recoveries, and deducts USD 574 million of trailing metal price lag; unadjusted EBITDA is USD 1,058 million [RQ2 p8, p9]. Management says it will stop excluding start-up costs once Bay Minette reaches normal capacity [Q2R p68].

The business model is a source of resilience with one concentration risk. Metal price passes through under the conversion model and volumes are supported by contracts of generally one to five years, but the 10 largest customers were 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales and Ball alone was 18% [business context; AR p23, p33, p188]. The parent has supported the build with USD 950 million of equity in fiscal 2026 and paid no return of capital in fiscal 2027 so far, but the filing states there is no assurance of further funding [business context; Q2R p61].

Structure and documentation limit how firmly guarantee and covenant questions can be answered. The notes are issued by Novelis Corporation and Novelis Sheet Ingot GmbH and guaranteed by Novelis Inc. and certain subsidiaries; non-guarantor subsidiaries held 20% of six-month net sales, 18% of Adjusted EBITDA and 11% of assets [Q2R p19, p64]. The only financial maintenance test described is a springing fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.25 to 1.0 on the revolver, which applies when excess availability falls below a threshold; availability of USD 606 million is above the highest value that threshold can take on the filed wording, but the June 2026 amendment text was not supplied [AR p148; financial base].

runs.text: Strengths. Scale and diversification support business risk: 29 facilities in nine countries, four segments that all contributed positive Adjusted EBITDA, and fiscal 2026 net sales of USD 18,434 million across beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace and specialty markets [business context; AR p8, p188]. The conversion model passes aluminum price to customers, so margin per tonne rather than metal price drives earnings [AR p73]. Recycling gives a metal cost lever: the company purchased or tolled about 2,155 kt of recycled aluminum against 1,298 kt of primary in fiscal 2026 [AR p18]. The company is current on all covenants and reports compliance with each facility at September 30, 2026 [Q2R p18 to p24]. The financial maintenance covenant package described is light: a single springing test on the revolver, with negative covenants in the notes and term loans and no other maintenance ratio described in the pages read [AR p146 to p148; Q2R p19]. Debt maturities are staggered, with no bond of size due before April 2029 [financial base]. The parent put in USD 950 million of equity in fiscal 2026 and has paid no return of capital this fiscal year [business context]. The efficiency plan had delivered over USD 200 million of run-rate savings at fiscal 2026 year end against a target of USD 350 million to USD 400 million by fiscal 2028 [Q2R p47].

Weaknesses. Net leverage of 4.7x is above management's 3.5x goal and gross debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 5.35x (calculated) [financial base]. Free cash flow is deeply negative: trailing Adjusted Free Cash Flow is an outflow of USD 3,682 million and operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 418 million in six months [financial base]. Liquidity is concentrated in a revolver that is mostly drawn, and short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million exceed cash of USD 1,277 million [financial base]. Interim cash interest is not disclosed, and accrual interest expense rose to USD 80 million in the quarter from USD 68 million [Q2R p3]. Customer concentration is high and rose year on year [AR p33]. Execution risk is live: the Bay Minette cold mill produced its first coil in September 2026, but commercial shipments are only targeted for the first quarter of fiscal 2028, so start-up costs and capital spending continue before the plant earns [RQ2 p2]. Insurance recoveries of USD 519 million cumulatively are real but further amounts and timing are uncertain [Q2R p48]. Trade measures matter: tariffs reduced fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by USD 143 million per the release, and the company announced a temporary production and staffing reduction at its Kingston, Canada plant because of duties [RQ4 p1; Q2R p47]. Floating rate debt exposes pre-tax income to about USD 15 million for each 100 basis points, on the company's stated sensitivity [Q2R p73]. Finally, the evidence on guarantee scope, covenant capacity and ratings is summary-level because no executed agreements or rating reports were supplied [source readiness].

runs.text: Financing activity over the last two fiscal years is a sequence of completed refinancings and new money for the Bay Minette programme, all described in the debt note. In fiscal 2025 the company issued 750 of 6.875% Senior Notes due January 2030 through Novelis Corporation and used the net proceeds to repay 738 of borrowings under the asset-based revolver (AR page:151), and entered a floating rate Term Loan Facility that provided 1,250 of proceeds and matures March 2032 (AR page:85; Q2R page:18); in September 2025 the term loan margin was cut from 2.00% to 1.75% over three-month Term SOFR (Q2R page:18). On August 18, 2025 Novelis Corporation issued 750 of 6.375% Senior Notes due August 2033 and used the net proceeds to buy 737 of the 750 outstanding 3.25% Senior Notes due November 2026 in a cash tender, leaving 13 outstanding (Q2R page:20; page:17). The Baldwin County Industrial Development Authority issued tax-exempt bonds loaned to Novelis Corporation to fund the Bay Minette plant: Series 2025A of 400 in June 2025 at 5.00%, Series 2025B of 100 in September 2025 at 4.625% and Series 2026A of 225 in March 2026 at 4.30%, each with a mandatory tender (June 2032 or March 2033) before final maturity (Q2R page:22 to page:24). The asset-based revolver was enlarged by 500 on February 19, 2026 to 2.5 billion and by a further 500 on June 16, 2026 to 3.0 billion, with maturity extended to June 16, 2031 (Q2R page:18). On July 23, 2026 the company signed an unsecured 500 term loan, fully drawn, due July 24, 2028 at Term SOFR plus 1.00% rising to 1.25% on certain rating events (Q2R page:21). Uncommitted trade and bank lines were added: a Citi facility of up to 300 after a January 2026 increase from 200, and an MUFG facility of up to 500 from May 26, 2026, both undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:19). Use of proceeds disclosed: bonds and the Bay Minette related issuance for construction costs, the 2033 notes for the tender of the 2026 notes, the March 2025 term loan to repay earlier term loans, and the 6.875% notes to repay revolver borrowings (Q2R page:18; page:20; page:22; AR page:151). The use of proceeds for the July 2026 term loan is Insufficient Information in the pages read.

Equity and distributions: the parent subscribed 950 of new shares in fiscal 2026 for capital projects (AR page:86; Q2R page:8), the company returned 35 of capital to the parent in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 and has paid none in fiscal 2027 (Q2R page:16). The Aditya Birla brand license from July 1, 2026 is a new related-party cost of up to 24 for fiscal 2027 (Q2R page:16).

Operating events with transaction-like effects: the Oswego fires of September 16 and November 20, 2025, with the hot mill restarting in early June 2026 and cumulative net insurance recoveries of 519 through September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:36; page:48); the June 2024 Sierre flood in Switzerland, financed in part by a CHF 100 million loan from the Banque Cantonale du Valais whose interest is payable by the Canton of Valais (Q2R page:21); restructuring under the 2025 Efficiency Plan with cumulative costs of 185 and a target of approximately 350 to 400 of annualized savings by the end of fiscal 2028 (Q2R page:47); and the Bay Minette plant, whose cold mill produced its first coil in September 2026 with commercial shipments targeted for the first quarter of fiscal 2028 (RQ2 page:2). The annual report said the plant was expected to commission in fiscal 2027 and in the second half of calendar 2026 (AR page:2; page:72), while the Q2 release reports a first coil in September 2026 and targets commercial shipments in the first quarter of fiscal 2028. These are different milestones, commissioning and commercial shipments, so no delay is concluded and no conflict is logged.

Subsequent events within the cutoff, after the quarter ended September 30, 2026: the board changes of November 3, 2026 (Q2R page:74); the 13 balance of the 3.25% notes falls due on November 15, 2026 by contract (AR page:150; Q2R page:17), which is a scheduled maturity and not a reported event; and the Q2 results release of November 5, 2026. No acquisition, disposal, sponsor change, rating action or new debt issue dated after September 30, 2026 was found in the supplied sources. No pending transaction is described.

fields.value: Novelis Inc. enters the latest quarter with higher leverage than a year earlier and thinner liquidity, while earnings are improving. Company-defined net leverage was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026 (RQ4 page:10; RQ2 page:10). The rise comes from the numerator: total debt principal grew from 6,212 at March 31, 2025 to 7,978 at March 31, 2026 and 9,797 at September 30, 2026 (AR page:145; Q2R page:17), while cash was 1,036, 1,254 and 1,277 at the same dates and trailing Adjusted EBITDA moved from 1,802 to 1,645 to 1,831. Cash used in operations was negative 418 in the six months ended September 30, 2026 against positive 411 a year earlier, and capital expenditure was 1,543 against 913 (Q2R page:4 to page:5), so the Bay Minette plant and the Oswego fires absorbed more cash than operations produced. The funding came from the asset-based revolver, which carried about 2.3 billion of borrowings at September 30, 2026 against 935 at March 31, 2026 (Q2R page:18 to page:19; AR page:146), a 500 term loan taken in July 2026 (Q2R page:21) and 950 of equity contributions from the parent in fiscal 2026 (AR page:111). Liquidity of 2,038 is 718 below the 2,756 at March 31, 2026; availability under committed facilities fell to 761 from 1,502 while cash rose to 1,277 from 1,254, and the filing attributes the decrease primarily to a higher revolver balance (Q2R page:61 to page:62). The latest quarter itself was strong on a reported basis: Adjusted EBITDA of 508 against 422 and net income of 210 against 163 (RQ2 page:9; Q2R page:3), but part of the Adjusted EBITDA gain is a 39 business interruption recovery and favorable metal and scrap effects that management itself cites (RQ2 page:2). Management expects capital spending to fall as Bay Minette moves to start-up and forecasts positive free cash flow and a start of deleveraging toward the end of fiscal 2027 (RQ2 page:3); that is a management expectation and is not used in any figure here.

fields.value: Novelis Inc. is a Canadian-incorporated, Atlanta-headquartered producer of aluminum rolled products that is wholly owned indirectly by Hindalco Industries Ltd. and files as a voluntary filer without public equity (AR page:1; page:2). Its model converts purchased primary and recycled metal into sheet, plate and foil for beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace and specialty customers, and passes metal price through to customers under a three-part price of an LME base, a local market premium and a conversion premium (AR page:73), so margin per tonne rather than metal price is the economic driver, and the open exposure is the timing difference called metal price lag (AR page:74). The creditor-relevant business facts are three. First, revenue is concentrated: the 10 largest customers were 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales against 41% in fiscal 2025, and one customer, Ball, was 18% (AR page:33; page:188). Second, the company is in the middle of a capital programme centered on a greenfield plant in Bay Minette, Alabama that management sizes at approximately 5.0 billion (AR page:72) and that the company says is funded through cash flows from operations and "a combination of local financing, our senior secured credit facilities, equity contributions from our common shareholder, and senior notes" (Q2R page:61), which is consistent with the rise in leverage and revolver usage shown in the financial base. Third, two fires at the Oswego plant in September and November 2025 idled the Oswego hot mill until its restart in early June 2026 and management estimated a total negative cash flow impact of approximately 1.7 billion before insurance (AR page:70; Q2R page:36); cumulative net insurance recoveries were 519 through September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:48). Ownership behavior in the filings is supportive on equity (950 of subscriptions at 150 a share in fiscal 2026) and mixed on distributions (a 35 return of capital in fiscal 2026 and a new brand royalty to an affiliate), and the filings give no signal of creditor-adverse transactions such as priming or drop-downs; that absence is an observation about the pages read, not proof of the legal capacity to do them, which depends on indenture and credit agreement terms that were not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financing activity over the last two fiscal years is a sequence of completed refinancings and new money for the Bay Minette programme, all described in the debt note. In fiscal 2025 the company issued 750 of 6.875% Senior Notes due January 2030 through Novelis Corporation and used the net proceeds to repay 738 of borrowings under the asset-based revolver (AR page:151), and entered a floating rate Term Loan Facility that provided 1,250 of proceeds and matures March 2032 (AR page:85; Q2R page:18); in September 2025 the term loan margin was cut from 2.00% to 1.75% over three-month Term SOFR (Q2R page:18). On August 18, 2025 Novelis Corporation issued 750 of 6.375% Senior Notes due August 2033 and used the net proceeds to buy 737 of the 750 outstanding 3.25% Senior Notes due November 2026 in a cash tender, leaving 13 outstanding (Q2R page:20; page:17). The Baldwin County Industrial Development Authority issued tax-exempt bonds loaned to Novelis Corporation to fund the Bay Minette plant: Series 2025A of 400 in June 2025 at 5.00%, Series 2025B of 100 in September 2025 at 4.625% and Series 2026A of 225 in March 2026 at 4.30%, each with a mandatory tender (June 2032 or March 2033) before final maturity (Q2R page:22 to page:24). The asset-based revolver was enlarged by 500 on February 19, 2026 to 2.5 billion and by a further 500 on June 16, 2026 to 3.0 billion, with maturity extended to June 16, 2031 (Q2R page:18). On July 23, 2026 the company signed an unsecured 500 term loan, fully drawn, due July 24, 2028 at Term SOFR plus 1.00% rising to 1.25% on certain rating events (Q2R page:21). Uncommitted trade and bank lines were added: a Citi facility of up to 300 after a January 2026 increase from 200, and an MUFG facility of up to 500 from May 26, 2026, both undrawn at September 30, 2026 (Q2R page:19). fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue durability. Evidence: supply contracts of "one to five years", a stated "high degree of renewal business" and significant switching costs (AR page:23) against a top 10 customer share of 57% in fiscal 2026 from 41% (AR page:33). Mechanism: long contracts and qualification costs support volume visibility, but a few customers hold most of the volume, so one non-renewal or insourcing decision moves a large share of revenue. Implication: revenue is durable in the base case and lumpy in the downside; the leverage tolerance of the credit is lower than the stable sector profile suggests.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin and earnings quality. Evidence: price pass-through under the conversion model (AR page:73) and adjustments for metal price lag, fire losses and start-up costs inside Adjusted EBITDA (RQ4 page:9). Mechanism: pass-through protects conversion margin against metal price moves, but timing gains and losses, fire items and start-up costs are excluded from the measure, so the measure and cash earnings can differ by large amounts in a period. Implication: leverage computed on Adjusted EBITDA should be read with the exclusions; the financial base carries both.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash flow and liquidity. Evidence: capital spending guidance of 2.1 to 2.4 billion for fiscal 2027 (Q2R page:48), negative operating cash flow for the six months (Q2R page:4) and revolver availability of 606 (Q2R page:19). Mechanism: the build continues for the rest of the year and start-up costs continue until normal capacity, while insurance recoveries are uncertain in amount and timing. Implication: refinancing and liquidity depend on revolver access and on delivery of management's expected return to positive free cash flow, which is a management expectation (RQ2 page:3).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: 950 of equity contributions and no fiscal 2027 distribution, against a new affiliate royalty. Mechanism: the parent has put in cash when the programme needed it; there is no stated obligation. Implication: treat parent support as demonstrated behavior, not a credit enhancement; the pages read contain no parent guarantee.

fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Novelis Inc. (issuer id novelis-inc), as of 2026-11-05, credit snapshot pathway. Scope is business risk, financial risk, liquidity, structure and the gaps that limit them, built from the accepted source-readiness, financial-base and business-context handoffs and checked against the filings. Amounts are USD millions and fiscal years end March 31.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Locators in brackets are the alias and the page chunk of the supplied extraction, for example [Q2R p17]. AR is the fiscal 2026 annual report; Q3R, Q1R and Q2R are the quarterly reports for the quarters ended December 31, 2025, June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2026; RQ4, RQ1 and RQ2 are the earnings releases of May 19, August 5 and November 5, 2026. Context source (settings, not issuer evidence): context, sha256 e98b858a20d2c069629867a63f74620ff3a26183f951dc5fd1ab64bb298a449a.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Novelis Inc. is a large, diversified aluminum rolling credit whose leverage and liquidity have weakened over the past six months, but it complies with its covenants and has no bond maturity of size before April 2029. The strongest support is a conversion pricing model that passes metal cost to customers, scale across four regions and a trailing Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,831 million. The weakest point is USD 9,797 million of debt, net leverage of 4.7x against a stated goal of 3.5x, USD 2,631 million of short-term borrowings and liquidity down to USD 2,038 million. The outcome turns on whether Bay Minette reaches commercial shipments, capital spending falls and insurance recoveries arrive, so that free cash flow turns positive.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Novelis Inc. has become more leveraged because it is funding a USD 5.0 billion plant and recovering from two fires at the same time. Company-defined net leverage was 2.9x at March 31, 2025, 4.1x at March 31, 2026 and 4.7x at September 30, 2026, against a management goal of about 3.5x during the investment cycle, which management says tariffs and the fire impacts have pushed above target [financial base; Q2R p65]. Total debt rose by USD 1,819 million in six months to USD 9,797 million, and Adjusted Net Debt rose by USD 1,796 million, almost the same as the USD 1,804 million Adjusted Free Cash Flow outflow, so the extra debt is the cash burn of capital spending and working capital rather than shareholder returns [financial base; RQ2 p9, p10].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity has narrowed and rests on one facility. The company had USD 2,038 million of liquidity at September 30, 2026, down from USD 2,756 million at March 31, 2026, and the revolver availability of USD 606 million is the main committed backstop [financial base; Q2R p19, p61]. The reported figures reconcile to a revolver drawn about USD 2,266 million with USD 128 million of letters of credit against a USD 3,000 million commitment (calculated, see Calculations), which suggests the commitment rather than the borrowing base is the binding limit; that is an inference and the borrowing base is not printed. Short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million are classified as due within one year, although the revolver itself matures on June 16, 2031 [Q2R p17, p18].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Bond maturities are not the near-term pressure. Only USD 13 million of 3.25% notes falls due in November 2026, and the next large maturities are USD 568 million of notes in April 2029, USD 2,350 million across two series in January 2030 and USD 750 million in August 2031 [financial base; Q2R p17]. The term loans mature in March 2032 and a USD 500 million term loan in July 2028. The risk is therefore the cost and availability of bank liquidity through the build, and then the size of the 2029 and 2030 refinancing if leverage has not come down.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings are improving on a reported basis but are definition sensitive. Trailing Adjusted EBITDA is USD 1,831 million against USD 1,645 million for fiscal 2026, and the quarter included USD 39 million of business interruption recoveries and favorable scrap effects that management cites [financial base; RQ2 p2]. The measure excludes USD 69 million of trailing start-up costs and USD 1,140 million of trailing fire losses net of recoveries, and deducts USD 574 million of trailing metal price lag; unadjusted EBITDA is USD 1,058 million [RQ2 p8, p9]. Management says it will stop excluding start-up costs once Bay Minette reaches normal capacity [Q2R p68].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business model is a source of resilience with one concentration risk. Metal price passes through under the conversion model and volumes are supported by contracts of generally one to five years, but the 10 largest customers were 57% of fiscal 2026 net sales and Ball alone was 18% [business context; AR p23, p33, p188]. The parent has supported the build with USD 950 million of equity in fiscal 2026 and paid no return of capital in fiscal 2027 so far, but the filing states there is no assurance of further funding [business context; Q2R p61].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure and documentation limit how firmly guarantee and covenant questions can be answered. The notes are issued by Novelis Corporation and Novelis Sheet Ingot GmbH and guaranteed by Novelis Inc. and certain subsidiaries; non-guarantor subsidiaries held 20% of six-month net sales, 18% of Adjusted EBITDA and 11% of assets [Q2R p19, p64]. The only financial maintenance test described is a springing fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.25 to 1.0 on the revolver, which applies when excess availability falls below a threshold; availability of USD 606 million is above the highest value that threshold can take on the filed wording, but the June 2026 amendment text was not supplied [AR p148; financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Scale and diversification support business risk: 29 facilities in nine countries, four segments that all contributed positive Adjusted EBITDA, and fiscal 2026 net sales of USD 18,434 million across beverage packaging, automotive, aerospace and specialty markets [business context; AR p8, p188]. The conversion model passes aluminum price to customers, so margin per tonne rather than metal price drives earnings [AR p73]. Recycling gives a metal cost lever: the company purchased or tolled about 2,155 kt of recycled aluminum against 1,298 kt of primary in fiscal 2026 [AR p18]. The company is current on all covenants and reports compliance with each facility at September 30, 2026 [Q2R p18 to p24]. The financial maintenance covenant package described is light: a single springing test on the revolver, with negative covenants in the notes and term loans and no other maintenance ratio described in the pages read [AR p146 to p148; Q2R p19]. Debt maturities are staggered, with no bond of size due before April 2029 [financial base]. The parent put in USD 950 million of equity in fiscal 2026 and has paid no return of capital this fiscal year [business context]. The efficiency plan had delivered over USD 200 million of run-rate savings at fiscal 2026 year end against a target of USD 350 million to USD 400 million by fiscal 2028 [Q2R p47].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Net leverage of 4.7x is above management's 3.5x goal and gross debt to Adjusted EBITDA is 5.35x (calculated) [financial base]. Free cash flow is deeply negative: trailing Adjusted Free Cash Flow is an outflow of USD 3,682 million and operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 418 million in six months [financial base]. Liquidity is concentrated in a revolver that is mostly drawn, and short-term borrowings of USD 2,631 million exceed cash of USD 1,277 million [financial base]. Interim cash interest is not disclosed, and accrual interest expense rose to USD 80 million in the quarter from USD 68 million [Q2R p3]. Customer concentration is high and rose year on year [AR p33]. Execution risk is live: the Bay Minette cold mill produced its first coil in September 2026, but commercial shipments are only targeted for the first quarter of fiscal 2028, so start-up costs and capital spending continue before the plant earns [RQ2 p2]. Insurance recoveries of USD 519 million cumulatively are real but further amounts and timing are uncertain [Q2R p48]. Trade measures matter: tariffs reduced fiscal 2026 Adjusted EBITDA by USD 143 million per the release, and the company announced a temporary production and staffing reduction at its Kingston, Canada plant because of duties [RQ4 p1; Q2R p47]. Floating rate debt exposes pre-tax income to about USD 15 million for each 100 basis points, on the company's stated sensitivity [Q2R p73]. Finally, the evidence on guarantee scope, covenant capacity and ratings is summary-level because no executed agreements or rating reports were supplied [source readiness].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: At September 30, 2026 cash was USD 1,277 million and availability under committed facilities USD 761 million, of which the revolver was USD 606 million with USD 128 million of letters of credit drawn on it [financial base; Q2R p19, p61]. The remaining USD 155 million of committed availability is not itemized in the pages read. Uncommitted Citi and MUFG facilities of up to USD 300 million and USD 500 million were undrawn and are not counted [Q2R p19]. Against this, USD 2,704 million of debt is due within one year, but USD 2,266 million of it is revolver borrowing (calculated) that matures in 2031 and USD 350 million is Brazil short-term loans, so the year-one figure is a rollover question rather than a scheduled repayment. Management's capital spending guidance of USD 2,100 million to USD 2,400 million for fiscal 2027 against USD 1,543 million spent in six months implies USD 557 million to USD 857 million in the second half (calculated). Operating cash flow for the second half is not guided in the filings, so no runway is computed. Seasonal or working capital swings matter: inventories rose to USD 5,145 million from USD 4,401 million and supplier finance programs hold USD 1.5 billion of confirmed invoices in payables [Q2R p3, p8].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant position. The notes and the term loans carry negative covenants and a cross-acceleration or cross-default feature; the Term Loan Facility cross-defaults to the revolver regardless of amount [Q2R p19, p20; AR p146]. Compliance is reported for every facility at September 30, 2026. The revolver springing fixed charge test is 1.25 to 1.0 and the company's own reported figure for it is not given; headroom cannot be stated, only that availability is above the highest the trigger can be [AR p148; financial base].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Secured debt under the senior secured credit facilities is the term loans of USD 1,231 million and the revolver of about USD 2,266 million, together USD 3,497 million (calculated), secured by substantially all assets of the company and the guarantors [AR p146]. The senior notes of USD 4,431 million and the tax-exempt bonds of USD 725 million are senior unsecured and guaranteed by Novelis Inc. and certain subsidiaries (calculated) [Q2R p17, p19, p22]; the USD 500 million 2026 term loan is unsecured, and its guarantors are not stated in the pages read [Q2R p21]. Non-guarantor subsidiaries held USD 3.7 billion of assets and USD 2.2 billion of debt and other liabilities including intercompany balances at September 30, 2026 [Q2R p65], which rank structurally ahead of the notes as to those subsidiaries' assets, although the figure includes intercompany balances. Outside the debt figure the company has operating lease liabilities of USD 112 million at March 31, 2026, accrued postretirement benefits of USD 449 million, estimated benefit payments of USD 1.2 billion through 2036, purchase obligations of USD 17.2 billion at March 31, 2026 of which USD 7.6 billion fall due within 12 months, supplier finance of USD 1.5 billion inside payables, factoring whose volume is not printed, and a cash deposit of about USD 127 million held against disputed U.S. antidumping duties [financial base; AR p84; Q2R p8, p39].
